newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds edge lower after Friday's surge.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds edge lower after Friday's surge.

text.p: Argentine bonds edged lower Monday afternoon, retreating from early highs as players felt prices were too strong after Friday's surge.
"There are probably better buying opportunities in stocks than bonds now," said a trader at a large foreign bank, pointing to the low yields of Argentine bonds after the gains of previous sessions.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.25 to 119.05, and Argentina's FRB due 2005 dipped 3/8 to 84-3/4.
Traders complained that extremely thin market activity added to the downward drift. Bonds were given a hefty boost Friday from lower-than-expected U.S. jobless figures.
"The real problem today was low volume," said another trader.
But the feeling was that dollar-denominated bonds were now slightly overbought, meaning there could be profit-taking in coming days.

As is often the case when dollar bonds reach highs, some traders suggested there was still some value in peso-denominated bonds that offer higher yields than dollar ones. The peso-denominated Bocon Previsional 1 due 2001 rose 0.22 to 112.10.
In the money market, call money rates fell to 6.68 percent from 6.88 percent.
